speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for presenting with gait and limb ataxia; given your significant medical history, I need to clarify your symptoms and background to narrow down the cause. Can you describe when these coordination issues started and if they worsen when you walk in the dark? Also, do you have any history of vitamin deficiencies, diabetes, or autoimmune disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of feeling "drunk" and clumsiness, particularly on the right side, strongly suggest a focal neurological lesion. Have you noticed any other changes on the right side, such as weakness, numbness, or facial drooping? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain.

text: The MRI confirms Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) with demyelinating lesions. Since PML is an opportunistic infection typically caused by severe immunosuppression, I must ask: Do you have HIV/AIDS or are you currently taking immunosuppressive medications for conditions like cancer or autoimmune diseases? REQUEST TEST: CD4 Count.

speaker: Doctor
